snake-game.name: Snake game
snake-game.blurb: Eat, grow and don't bite your tail.

solitaire.a1: Move all 52 cards to the four foundations, one suit each from ace to king. In the seven piles you build down in alternating colours (a red 6 on a black 7), and only a king can fill an empty pile. Tap the stock to turn over new cards.
solitaire.q2: What is the difference between draw 1 and draw 3?
solitaire.a2: Draw 1 turns one card at a time and is easier. Draw 3 turns three and lets you play only the top one, which is the classic, harder game.
solitaire.a3: No. Some Klondike deals cannot be solved however you play. If you are stuck, undo a few moves or start a new deal.
solitaire.q4: How do I move cards quickly?
solitaire.a4: Double-click a card, or tap it twice, to send it to the best place: a foundation if it fits there, otherwise a pile. Once every card is face up and the stock is empty, the game finishes itself.
solitaire.a5: Yes. Every deal has a number. Restart plays the same deal again, and you can type a number to play a particular deal. Your game in progress is kept in this browser.

spider-solitaire.q1: How do you play spider solitaire?
spider-solitaire.a1: Build runs from king down to ace in one suit. A finished run leaves the table; clear all eight to win. You can place any card on a card one rank higher, but only a run in one suit moves as a group.
spider-solitaire.a2: One suit is the easiest and most games can be won. Two suits is a real challenge, and four suits is hard even for experienced players.
spider-solitaire.q3: When can I deal from the stock?
spider-solitaire.a3: Tap the stock to deal one card on each of the ten piles. You have five deals, and every pile must hold at least one card before you deal.
spider-solitaire.a4: Yes, as many times as you like, including after a deal.
spider-solitaire.a5: Yes. Close the page and come back later to the same game, moves and time. Nothing is sent to cv.cm.

freecell.a1: All cards are dealt face up into eight columns. Move them to the four foundations by suit from ace to king. Build columns down in alternating colours, and use the four free cells to park one card each.
freecell.q2: How many cards can I move at once?
freecell.a2: As many as the free space allows: one more than the number of empty free cells, doubled for every empty column. The page shows the current number.
freecell.a3: Almost. Of the first 32,000 classic deals only number 11982 has no solution.
freecell.q4: Are these the same deal numbers as other FreeCell games?
freecell.a4: Yes. Deals are made with the traditional numbering formula, so game 1 here is the game 1 known from other FreeCell programs.
freecell.q5: Why do some cards move by themselves?
freecell.a5: Cards that can no longer be needed in the columns go to the foundations automatically, as in most FreeCell programs. Undo brings them back.

minesweeper.a1: Open squares one at a time. A number tells how many mines touch that square, including diagonally. Use the numbers to work out where the mines are, flag them, and open every square without a mine to win.
minesweeper.a2: Yes. The mines are laid after your first click, and never on that square or the eight around it, so the first click always opens an area.
minesweeper.q3: How do I place a flag on a phone?
minesweeper.a3: Press and hold a square, or turn on Flag mode so that every tap places or removes a flag. On a computer, right-click.
minesweeper.a4: When a number already has that many flags around it, click the number to open all its other neighbours at once. If a flag is wrong, a mine goes off.
minesweeper.a5: Beginner is 9 × 9 with 10 mines, intermediate 16 × 16 with 40, and expert 30 × 16 with 99. Custom boards go up to 30 rows and 40 columns.

snake-game.a1: Steer the snake to the food. Each piece makes it one square longer. The game ends when the snake hits a wall or its own tail.
snake-game.a2: Use the arrow keys or W A S D, swipe on the board, or tap the arrow buttons. Space or P pauses.
snake-game.q3: What does turning walls off do?
snake-game.a3: Without walls, the snake leaves one side of the board and comes back on the opposite side. Only its own tail can end the game.
snake-game.q4: Why does my turn not happen?
snake-game.a4: The snake cannot turn straight back into itself. Up to two quick turns are remembered, so you can turn twice between steps.
snake-game.a5: Yes, in this browser only, with a separate best for each speed and wall setting.

solitaire.lead: Play Klondike solitaire in three steps.
solitaire.s1b: Pick draw 1 (easier) or draw 3 (classic) and tap New game.
solitaire.s2b: Drag or tap cards to stack them down in alternating colours. Tap the stock for new cards.
solitaire.s3b: Send each suit home from ace to king. Double-click a card to move it to its best place.

spider-solitaire.lead: Play spider solitaire in three steps.
spider-solitaire.s1b: One suit is the easiest; two and four suits are harder.
spider-solitaire.s2b: Place cards on a card one rank higher and move same-suit runs together.
spider-solitaire.s3b: A king-to-ace run in one suit leaves the table. Tap the stock to deal when you need new cards.

freecell.s1b: Tap New game, or type a deal number and tap Play deal.
freecell.s2b: Park single cards in the four cells and build columns down in alternating colours.
freecell.s3b: Move every suit to the foundations from ace to king. Safe cards go there by themselves.

minesweeper.s1b: Pick a level and click any square. The first click always opens a safe area.
minesweeper.s2b: Each number counts the mines around it. Flag mines with a right-click, a long press or Flag mode.
minesweeper.s3b: Open every square without a mine to win. Click a number with all its flags placed to open the rest.

snake-game.s1b: Tap Start or press Space. Choose a speed and whether the walls are on.
snake-game.s2b: Steer with the arrow keys, a swipe or the buttons. Each piece of food adds a point and one square.
snake-game.s3t: Avoid the walls and your tail
snake-game.s3b: Hitting a wall or your own body ends the game. Your best score is kept.
